newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil weak on supply, crude futures.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil weak on supply, crude futures.

text.p: NWE high sulphur fuel oil was weaker on Monday as crude oil futures took another tumble and amid a still-healthy supply situation in northwest Europe, traders said.
High sulphur barges traded in the morning at $88 a tonne fob ARA and then prices slipped, trading at $85 and $86 amid very thin demand for bunker fuel.

High sulphur cargoes slipped notionally after business was concluded at $92 cif NWE on Friday. Dealers said numbers had slipped by around two or three dollars a tonne on Monday, but fixed price talk was scant.
An ARA refiner who was offering a high sulphur cargo on Friday said he was no longer offering on Monday and would keep his product within his own system.
Low sulphur fuel oil was also weaker alongside crude oil and supply remains good.

An Italian refiner was heard to still have a little interest for early March barrels. Otherwise, end user demand was hard to pin down. Dealers pegged physical prices close to swaps levels, at around $93/$94 fob NWE.
